name: CO-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Denver-based district with a 29-point Democratic partisan lean
Kiros raised about $1.1M while Peterson raised roughly $2K
Open seat after DeGette lost renomination, but party advantage holds
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97%
model.rationale: A 29-point Democratic district, a roughly 500-to-1 fundraising gap in Kiros's favor, and market pricing near 97 percent all point to a comfortable Democratic hold despite the open seat; the absence of polls and the crowded minor-party field add uncertainty about the margin, not the winner.
model.watch: A late scandal, unusually strong third-party or independent turnout, or a lopsided Republican-leaning national environment could narrow the margin, though not plausibly flip the result.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Diana DeGette (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Denver's House seat is among the most Democratic districts in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 29 points toward Democrats. Longtime incumbent Diana DeGette will not appear on the ballot after losing renomination, creating an open seat, but Democratic nominee Melat Kiros carries the district's underlying advantage into the general election. Kiros raised about $1.1 million and attracted substantial outside spending from both supporters and opponents, while Republican Christy Peterson raised roughly $2,000 and has run a minimal campaign. A Libertarian, an Independent, and another minor candidate are also on the ballot.

Prediction markets put Democratic odds around 97 percent, and no general-election polling indicates a competitive race. The realistic question is the size of the winning margin rather than the winner, with third-party vote share and turnout the main variables to watch.
